approach: A `cargo` symlink to the athena binary sits in a per-job wrapper directory that is first on the producer's PATH. `main` sees argv[0] is `cargo`; for build, check, clippy, test, doc and run it calls `slot_exec::run`, the same function behind the hidden `athena build-slot --settings <f> -- <cmd>` subcommand. `run` takes a producer-class slot from the real `SlotQueue`, writes one JSON log line for every slotted command it handles (outcome `ran` with queued_s and slots held, or `timed_out` with the seconds waited), and runs the command as a plain child in the wrapper's own process group. The child env carries `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD=1` so a nested cargo passes through. A wait past the limit prints `no build slot free for <N> s; try again` and exits 75. The slot is a file lock, so the OS frees it on any exit. If `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT` is absent (a process whose env was rebuilt, such as a check command), the wrapper passes through to the real cargo and logs nothing; the hook is the fail-closed point for producers. The wait limit is `min(build_wait_s, bash_default_timeout_ms/1000 − 60)`. The producer-role policy denies a slotted cargo unless the first `cargo` on the hook's PATH is the wrapper. `invoke_and_record` reads and removes the wrapper log into an optional `Invocation.build_slots`; `slotted_seen` is counted with the policy tokenizer. The 'build wait' line adds producer waits (timed-out ones included, counted separately), the peak slots held and an unslotted note that now means only 'never reached the wrapper'. Producer commands only; no unsafe code; no non-Rust file.

decisions.choice: The wrapper is a symlink named `cargo` to the athena binary, dispatched on argv[0] in `main` beside the existing `pre-commit`/`commit-msg` dispatch (main.rs ~546-553). A hidden clap variant `build-slot --settings <f> -- <cmd>` calls the same `slot_exec::run`.
decisions.reason: No shell script is needed (Rust-only default). `-- <cmd>` is the form the design names; tests and the wrapper share one code path.

rejected.option: A `#!/bin/sh` wrapper script that execs `athena build-slot -- cargo "$@"`
rejected.why: It adds a non-Rust file and needs its own recursion guard.

rejected.option: Having the hook rewrite the command to `athena build-slot -- cargo ...`
rejected.why: It needs new hook output and changes what commands_run holds. The design says a PATH wrapper.

decisions.choice: Re-entrancy and missing settings (answers finding 11). `run` sets `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD=1` in the child's env; `cargo_wrapper` checks it first and passes through with no slot and no log line. If `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT` is absent, `cargo_wrapper` also passes through to the real cargo with no slot and no log line. If it is set but the file is unreadable or not valid settings, the wrapper exits 1 with a message naming the file (a broken install must not run unslotted). Producers are still fail-closed because the hook denies a slotted cargo when `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_BIN` is missing (decision 7). Every slot_exec test builds its child Command through one helper `scrubbed()` (env_clear, explicit PATH, only the slot variables the test needs). `real_cargo` takes PATH and its own path as arguments and skips PATH entries whose `cargo` canonicalizes to the running binary.
decisions.reason: checks.rs:447-450 runs check commands with `env_clear().envs(ctx.env)` and env::build passes PATH (athena.toml:52 env_pass) but not the slot variables, so a nested athena check under a producer's `cargo test` sees the wrapper first on PATH with no settings; exit 1 would break it, and the hook already guarantees the variable for producers, so failing closed in the wrapper adds no protection. Repo tests start `cargo` by name (slots.rs:824, run/tests.rs:2659, disk.rs:824, xtask/tests/ci_shards.rs:121); with max_check_slots = 1 (config.rs:165) a nested cargo would wait for a second slot and time out, hence the HELD marker. Tests must not inherit the marker (crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs:289-291 does the same for ATHENA_NESTED). The policy denies `NAME=value` prefixes (policy.rs:546-553), so a producer cannot set the marker.

rejected.option: Exit 1 when ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT is absent (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Breaks any process that inherits the wrapper PATH with a rebuilt env, and protects nothing the hook does not already protect.

rejected.option: Remove the wrapper dir from the child's PATH
rejected.why: String-edits PATH and stops later nested calls from being checked.

rejected.option: Let tests inherit the process env
rejected.why: CI passes (no wrapper) while every later producer's run of these tests would fail.

decisions.choice: The child is a plain `Command::spawn` in the wrapper's own process group: no `procs::isolate`, no signal handler. Exit code is the child's, or 128+signal.
decisions.reason: procs.rs:88-92 `isolate` moves the child to a new group, so group kills (Registry::stop_all, kill_group on deadline) would miss rustc and test binaries. `unsafe_code = deny` rules out a new signal handler outside procs.rs.

rejected.option: procs::isolate
rejected.why: Takes the build tree out of the agent's group.

rejected.option: A pub parent-death helper in procs.rs
rejected.why: procs.rs is not a deliverable; the gap (wrapper alone SIGKILLed) is stated in the Built note.

decisions.choice: The wrapper reads its queue from `{job_dir}/build-slot.json` (slots dir, slots, wait_s, promote_s), named by env `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT`; log path in `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG`; wrapper dir in `ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_BIN`. `SlotSettings::producer(dir, &pipeline, bash_default_timeout_ms)` caps wait_s at `bash_default_timeout_ms/1000 − 60` (min 1) and keeps `promote_s = build_age_promote_s` unchanged.
decisions.reason: config.rs:166 gives 1800 s, athena.toml:64-65 sets Bash timeouts of 600 s/1200 s, env.rs:81-88 passes them to the agent. A wrapper that waits 1800 s is killed first by the Bash tool and the producer never sees the message. The agent's ATHENA_STATE_DIR is the nested job state (env.rs:97-100), so the shared slots dir must be written down; EnvSpec is built in about ten places so it gets no new fields. promote_s is not changed per role: is_head (slots.rs:298-308) orders every ticket with the reader's own promote, so processes using different intervals disagree on the head and waiters could stall. The cap covers only the default Bash timeout (finding 12): the Bash timeout spans wait plus run, so a producer that passes a shorter `timeout`, or wins a slot near the cap and then runs more than about 60 s, is killed by the tool and never sees the message. The OS frees the slot at once because the group is killed. The Built note says so in one sentence.

rejected.option: Write build_wait_s unchanged
rejected.why: The shipped config could not show the behavior asked for.

rejected.option: Give the producer its own smaller promote_s
rejected.why: Readers with different intervals disagree on which ticket is head (slots.rs:298-308); waiters could stall to timeout.

rejected.option: New fields on EnvSpec
rejected.why: Forces edits at every EnvSpec literal.

decisions.choice: Cap versus ageing: state it, pin it with a pure test, ask. Add `SlotSettings::ages_into_check_class(&self) -> bool` (true when wait_s >= promote_s, the point where a Producer ticket ties a Check ticket under `effective = class − age/promote`, slots.rs:298-308). A slots.rs test shows it is false for the shipped numbers (wait 540 < promote 600) and true for an uncapped 1800 s wait. The Risks, the Built note and CHANGELOG say: a retry makes a new ticket with a fresh queued_at (slots.rs:245-251), so retries never build up age, and with max_check_slots = 1 and a steady stream of checks a producer can wait to exit 75 without promotion. A User question asks for `build_age_promote_s` below the cap in a governance job.
decisions.reason: The design (agent-and-build-slots.md:155-156) says ageing keeps the producer class from starving behind checks. The Bash timeout cap makes a wait past the promote interval impossible with the shipped numbers. The fix lies in governance config (athena.toml is out of scope); the plan must not hide the loss.

rejected.option: Per-role promote_s in the producer's settings
rejected.why: Breaks head agreement between processes (decision 4).

rejected.option: Raise the cap above the Bash timeout
rejected.why: The producer never sees the exit 75 message.

rejected.option: Warn at runtime in the wrapper
rejected.why: The check is static and belongs in a test and the docs.

decisions.choice: Age carry across retries (finding 10) is considered and not built. The Built note states why: it needs an enqueue variant in slots.rs that takes a given queued_at, a per-job file holding the first unanswered ask, and a staleness rule. Without the rule a producer that gave up and returned much later would arrive with a huge age and jump ahead of checks, and any rule needs a new time constant. It also makes ordering depend on the producer's retry habit. The User question on build_age_promote_s stays.
decisions.reason: Small-change default: step 4 of section 8 does not name it, and the anti-starvation rule can be restored by one governance value instead of new state and a new constant.

rejected.why: New state, a staleness rule with a new constant, a slots.rs enqueue variant and a stale-file hazard after SIGKILL, for a problem one config value fixes.

rejected.why: `cargo run` and `cargo doc` would compile outside the limit.

decisions.choice: The wrapper rule is read from the environment, not a new `Policy` field. In policy.rs a private `enum BuildWrapper { NotRequired, Required { dir: Option<PathBuf>, path: Option<OsString> } }` is built by `BuildWrapper::from_env(role, lookup)`: Required for `Role::Producer`, NotRequired otherwise. `evaluate` keeps its signature and calls `evaluate_in(policy, tool, input, cwd, &BuildWrapper)`; `check_bash`, `check_segment`, `check_cargo` gain the argument. For Required and `takes_build_slot(sub)`, deny unless `dir` is Some, `<dir>/cargo` is a file, and the first PATH directory holding a file `cargo` is `dir` (canonicalized). The test helper `bash` uses NotRequired. A missing variable denies (fails closed).
decisions.reason: Existing denials (`/usr/bin/cargo`, `./cargo`, `+nightly`, `--target-dir`) already exist; the new rule must catch a different cargo winning PATH. Reading env leaves `Policy` unchanged, which avoids literal edits in admission.rs, run/planning.rs, tests/refusal_corpus.rs and tests/live.rs (every Policy literal outside policy.rs and reading.rs is a Verifier policy: refusal_corpus.rs:1030/1191, admission.rs:688/818/903, planning.rs:219, live.rs:170). The hook inherits the agent's env (hooks.rs:52-78).

The reading.rs test asserts the pair.

decisions.choice: Keep `commands_run: Vec<String>`. Add one optional sibling `Invocation.build_slots: Option<BuildSlots>` with `BuildSlots { commands: Vec<CommandSlot>, slotted_seen: u32 }` and `CommandSlot { subcommand: String, queued_s: f64, slots_held: u32, outcome: SlotOutcome }`, where `SlotOutcome` is `ran` or `timed_out` (serde snake_case); all three types deny unknown fields; `build_slots` is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.

rejected.why: Changes every reader and the old-record read path.

decisions.choice: Every slotted command the wrapper handles leaves one log line (answers finding 7). Won slot: the line is written right after the win and before the child spawns, outcome `ran`, queued_s from the wrapper's own `Instant`, slots_held from `Slot::held()`. Timeout: on SlotWait the wrapper writes outcome `timed_out`, queued_s = seconds actually waited (at least the limit), slots_held 0, then prints the message and exits 75. Pass-through cases (HELD marker, no settings, non-slotted subcommand) write nothing. `slotted_seen` is compared with all logged lines, so the unslotted note means only 'a slotted cargo command in commands_run never reached the wrapper'. The 'build wait' line folds timed-out waits into the producer count, total and longest, and adds `N timed out`.
decisions.reason: Timeouts are the longest waits; the design (agent-and-build-slots.md:410-411) measures the effect by producer queued_s, and leaving them out biases the line low. Without a timed_out line every exit 75 would show up as a bypass and the note would lose its meaning (the Bash-tool PATH check, Host question).

rejected.option: Log only after a slot is won (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Drops the worst waits and flags each exit 75 as an unslotted command.

rejected.option: A third outcome `no_settings`
rejected.why: Decision 2 makes a missing settings variable a pass-through that logs nothing; a set-but-broken file exits 1 before any slot work.

decisions.choice: The unslotted count is built on the policy tokenizer (answers finding 9). In policy.rs add `pub fn slotted_cargo_commands(commands: &[String]) -> usize`, re-exported from athena-agent lib.rs: for each string run `tokenize`, split on `Token::Separator` as check_bash does (policy.rs:495-512), and count segments whose first word is exactly `cargo` and whose subcommand (`cargo_subcommand`, skipping leading dash words the way check_cargo does) satisfies `takes_build_slot`. A string `tokenize` rejects counts 0 (the policy would deny it, so it never ran). `invoke_and_record` calls pure `build_slots_record(log_text: Option<&str>, commands_run: &[String])`; the record is None when there is no log and nothing seen. Status skips the note when the invocation's `driver.name == "fake"` (athena-agent/src/fake.rs:82; reading.rs:408 uses the same test), because the fake driver runs no real PATH resolution and its tests list `cargo test` (run/tests.rs:4805).
decisions.reason: One tokenizer for both policy and count: quoted text such as `git log --grep 'cargo build; x'` is not miscounted. The record states what was seen; the reader decides whether a mismatch is meaningful.

rejected.why: Miscounts quoted text; a second parser beside the one the policy trusts.

decisions.choice: The note's limits are stated truthfully (answers finding 8). commands_run excludes denied commands when the result event arrives (stream.rs:154-166, `denied_tool_use_ids`; invocation.rs:152-159), so the note does not claim denied commands are counted. The only overcount named is a killed invocation, whose commands come from the partial sink (invocation.rs:75-80, stream.rs `bash` list) and may include a command that was started and denied or never ran. The strings are redacted before they reach the record, which the count does not depend on. The Built note, Risks and status text carry only this.

decisions.choice: Exit 75 with the documented message plus a `timed_out` log line is the whole timeout handling for producer commands; no hold marker is written. 'Held, not failed' is read as: the producer's job is not failed and no attempt is spent. The design (agent-and-build-slots.md:164-165) leaves the decision to the producer after exit 75. The gap with the request's 'held' is a User question and is stated in the Built note and CHANGELOG. 'Not failed' is shown by an invocation.rs test (decision 14) and by the argument that no code path turns a command's exit code into job state; the wrapper has no job-state access.

rejected.option: Writing a slot-wait hold marker from the wrapper

decisions.choice: The peak is carried per producer command as `slots_held`: `Slot::held()` counts locked slot files just after the slot is won. The status line prints the maximum, labelled 'when a producer command started' (a lower bound). Tests assert `overlap <= limit`, `held <= limit` and `max held >= forced overlap`, never exact equality except at a barrier. Overlap is forced by barriers and measured apart from the lock files; a control runs the same commands unwrapped and must read overlap above the limit.
decisions.reason: A count over N lock files is at most N by construction, so 'held <= limit' alone cannot fail. Equality is flaky (a holder may decrement before it drops its lock); a forced barrier makes `>=` deterministic.

rejected.option: Assert Slot::held() <= limit only
rejected.why: True by construction.

The criterion 3 demonstration says plainly that this shows the record path does not turn a recorded command, even a timed-out one, into a failure, and that the exit-75-holds-nothing half is a design argument.
decisions.reason: The criterion names the behavior; a cheap test covers what can be reached without step-3 files, and the rest is stated so the verifier does not expect a test.

rejected.option: A run/tests.rs run-level test
rejected.why: run/tests.rs is a step-3 file, out of scope.

risks.risk: The host's hook or Bash tool resolves PATH differently from the environment built here, so `cargo` runs the real cargo unslotted.
risks.mitigation: The hook denies a slotted cargo unless the first `cargo` on its own PATH is the wrapper and the variable is present (fails closed). If only the Bash tool differs, `slotted_seen` in the record exceeds the logged lines (ran plus timed_out) and `athena status` says so on the first real run. The Built note says hook/Bash equality was not measured.

risks.risk: If the hook process does not inherit the agent's env, every slotted producer cargo is denied.
risks.mitigation: The denial reason names the missing variable. fmt, metadata and tree stay allowed. Recorded as the Host question.

risks.risk: Starvation: the producer wait cap (540 s) is below build_age_promote_s (600 s), so a producer ticket never promotes into the check class, and a retry gets a fresh ticket with no age (slots.rs:245-251). With max_check_slots = 1, a steady stream of checks can starve producers to exit 75.
risks.mitigation: promote_s is left equal for every process (head agreement). The property is pinned by a slots.rs test and stated in the Built note and CHANGELOG. Age carry was weighed and rejected (new state, staleness rule, new constant). The User question asks for a governance change to build_age_promote_s. Producers get a clear exit 75 and may retry; checks hold slots briefly.

risks.risk: Wrapper install (reading.rs) and PATH env (env.rs) could diverge and deny every slotted cargo, or install an unused wrapper.
risks.mitigation: Both gate on `side == Side::Produce`; the reading.rs pair test checks the Side::Produce spec has the wrapper and variables and others do not; the policy keys on Role::Producer, and run/producer.rs:166 is the only Side::Produce caller.

risks.risk: A cargo started inside a slotted command takes a second slot and times out.
risks.mitigation: ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_HELD makes nested wrappers pass through; the nested test with slots=1 fails without it. The policy denies `NAME=value` prefixes (policy.rs:546), so the agent cannot set the marker.

risks.risk: A process that inherits the wrapper PATH with a rebuilt env (a check command) runs cargo unslotted because ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT is absent.
risks.mitigation: That is intended (finding 11): such processes are not producer commands, and the hook already denies a producer's slotted cargo when its variables are missing. The pass-through test covers it; the Built note names it.

risks.risk: New tests inherit slot variables when a later producer runs them through its own wrapper.
risks.mitigation: All children go through `scrubbed()`; `real_cargo` takes explicit arguments; `slot_exec_tests_do_not_inherit_the_slot_variables` fails if the scrub is dropped.

risks.risk: If the wrapper alone is SIGKILLed, its child cargo keeps running without a slot.
risks.mitigation: Group kills (athena stop, deadlines) reach the whole tree because the child stays in the agent's group; test (d) checks it. The single-process-kill gap is stated in the Built note.

risks.risk: Counting held slots briefly try-locks free slot files and can make another waiting head miss a slot for one poll (250 ms).
risks.mitigation: The count runs only after a win; cost is at most one poll of extra wait; tests use `>=`/`<=` with forced barriers; the Built note mentions it.

risks.risk: The recorded peak is sampled only at producer-command starts, so it can undercount.
risks.mitigation: The status line labels it 'when a producer command started'; the Built note calls it a lower bound; the overlap test measures real concurrency.

risks.risk: Slots held for `cargo run` and `cargo test` last as long as the program runs and can block checks for up to the Bash timeout (athena.toml:65).
risks.mitigation: Stated as a known cost in the Built note; the wait cap bounds other waiters, who get 75 or a held check.

risks.risk: The wait cap protects only the default Bash timeout: a producer that passes a shorter Bash `timeout`, or wins a slot near the cap and then runs more than about 60 s, is killed by the Bash tool and never sees the documented message.
risks.mitigation: The slot is freed by the OS when the group is killed; one sentence in the Built note states both cases. Not measured.

risks.risk: A producer retries in a loop after exit 75.
risks.mitigation: The message says to try again later; each timeout leaves a timed_out line with its wait, so the status line shows the count and the longest wait.

risks.risk: The unslotted count can overcount: for a killed invocation the commands come from the partial sink and may include a command that was denied or never ran.
risks.mitigation: For completed invocations denied commands are already excluded (stream.rs:154-166). The note is skipped for the fake driver. `slotted_cargo_commands` uses the policy tokenizer and has unit tests for `&&`, `;`, `|`, quoted text and `cargo fmt --check`.

risks.risk: The tokenizer reads redacted command strings; redaction could change a command word.
risks.mitigation: Redaction replaces secret-like values, not the leading program and subcommand; a changed string would only undercount, which is stated in the Built note.

risks.risk: The timeout test needs a real wait of about one second because wait_s is in whole seconds.
risks.mitigation: wait_s = 1 and bounded 10 s poll loops; no sleeps order events.

risks.risk: Stale settings or log files from an earlier invocation of the same job (send-back passes).
risks.mitigation: `agent_spec` rewrites the settings and wrapper on each producer invocation; `invoke_and_record` removes a stale log before the run and the log after it; a test covers the stale log.

risks.risk: Invocation literals outside the deliverable list are missed.
risks.mitigation: The edits are listed by file and line; `cargo test --locked` and clippy fail on any missed literal.

risks.risk: Scope: six files outside the listed deliverables change (findings 1-6).
risks.mitigation: Each is the only place that can do its job or a compile-forced one-line literal (decision 15); the Built note names each and why; no step-3 file and no governance file changes.

demonstrations.method: Integration tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/slot_exec.rs, names prefixed `slot_exec_`, run the real athena binary (env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_athena")) against a real SlotQueue over the same temp dir with limit 1 and probe with `SlotQueue::try_acquire`. Every child Command goes through `scrubbed()`. (a) `athena build-slot --settings <f> -- sh -c 'touch started; wait for release'`: after `started` appears try_acquire is None; after release and exit it is Some. (b) A symlink `bin/cargo` to the athena binary and a fake real `cargo` script written at run time into another temp dir, PATH=bin:real: `cargo build`, `test`, `clippy` and `check` each hold the slot while running and free it after; `cargo fmt --check` does not hold it and writes no log line. (c) A command that runs `kill -KILL $$`: wrapper exit 137 and the slot is free. (d) The wrapper in its own process group with `sh -c 'sleep 30 & sleep 30'`; the test calls `athena_agent::procs::kill_group(pgid, GRACE)`; the slot is free and `group_alive(pgid)` is false within a bounded 10 s poll. (e) Re-entrancy: slots=1, wait_s=5, `build-slot -- sh -c 'cargo build'` with PATH=bin:real exits 0 well before 5 s and the log has one line. (f) `slot_exec_cargo_without_settings_passes_through`: scrubbed env without ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT, PATH=bin:real, `cargo build` runs the fake real cargo, exits 0, writes no log, takes no slot; a settings variable naming a missing file exits 1. (g) `slot_exec_tests_do_not_inherit_the_slot_variables`: variables set before `scrubbed()` are absent from `sh -c env`. Unit tests in slot_exec.rs call `real_cargo(path, self_path)` with explicit arguments.

demonstrations.method: Test `slot_exec_second_producer_waits_for_the_first_then_runs`: settings slots=1. Wrapper A runs `sh -c 'touch a_started; wait for release; touch a_ended'`. After `a_started`, wrapper B (own log file) runs `sh -c 'test -e a_ended && touch b_ran_after_a'`. Poll (10 s deadline) until `SlotQueue::waiting() == 1`; assert `b_ran_after_a` is absent. Create `release`; wait for both. Assert `b_ran_after_a` exists, B exited 0, and B's log line has outcome `ran`, queued_s > 0 and slots_held == 1. A second test `slot_exec_peak_is_bounded_by_the_limit`: slots=2, three wrappers; A and B each wait for the other's start marker so they overlap, C queues behind. Commands append start/end marks to one shared file and the test computes the greatest overlap. Assert overlap == 2 (forced), C starts after one ended, and the largest slots_held in the logs is >= 2 and <= 2. A control runs three unwrapped commands the same way and must read overlap above 2.
demonstrations.observes: B waits behind A, runs only after A's command ended, and its recorded queued_s is above zero; no more than the limit run at once.

demonstrations.method: Test groups. (1) records.rs: an old Invocation JSON without `build_slots` reads with None and writes without the key; one with entries (outcomes ran and timed_out) round-trips; an unknown key inside BuildSlots or CommandSlot is refused. (2) status.rs: invocations carrying `build_slots` (ran with queued 3.0 and 5.0, slots_held 1 and 2) plus checks with queued_s give a 'build wait' line with `over N check(s) and M producer command(s), longest ... s` and `peak 2 slot(s) held at once when a producer command started`; one `timed_out` line (queued_s 540) is counted in M, in the longest, and shown as `1 timed out`, and with slotted_seen equal to the logged lines gives no unslotted note; slotted_seen 3 with 1 logged line adds the unslotted note; the same record with `driver.name == "fake"` gives no note; the existing `over 2 check(s), longest 30.0 s` test stays valid and no recorded waits gives no line. (3) slots.rs: four threads on a real queue with limit 2 take and release slots; a `std::sync::Barrier` forces two to hold at once; a shared AtomicUsize measures overlap. Assert overlap == 2 at the barrier, overlap <= 2 always, every `Slot::held()` <= 2, max held >= 2; a control runs the same threads without acquiring and must reach overlap above 2. (4) tests/slot_exec.rs peak test of criterion 2. (5) invocation.rs: with the fake driver the test writes a log at the path in `spec.env[ATHENA_BUILD_SLOT_LOG]` before `invoke_and_record`; the record has the parsed `build_slots.commands` and the file is gone; a stale log written before the call is not read. Pure `build_slots_record` tests: a string such as `cargo test && cargo fmt --check; cargo build` with no log gives slotted_seen 2, `cargo fmt --check` alone gives None. `slotted_cargo_commands` unit tests in policy.rs: `&&`, `;`, `|`, newline, `cargo -q build`, a quoted `git log --grep 'cargo build; x'` counts 0, `echo cargo test` counts 0, an untokenizable string counts 0.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-data && cargo test -p athena-core status && cargo test -p athena-core slots && cargo test -p athena-core invocation && cargo test -p athena-agent && cargo test -p athena-cli slot_exec
demonstrations.observes: queued_s stored per producer command, timeouts included; old records still read; the status line carries producer waits, timeouts, the peak and the unslotted note (only for commands that never reached the wrapper); the peak never passes the limit, measured by overlap apart from the lock files; a bypass is visible in the record; the fake driver gives no note.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the field, an invocation JSON with build_slots fails to parse (deny_unknown_fields). Without the status change the line lacks producer and peak text. Without the queue (an unwrapped run) the overlap instrument reads above the limit, so the limit assertion can fail. Without consuming the log, build_slots stays None. Without the seen-count, the bypass note test fails; if timed_out lines were not logged, the timeout status test shows a false note. Without the fake-driver skip in status, the fake case prints the note.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `Throughput::compute(...).text()`, `SlotQueue::acquire` and `Slot::held` (step 1), `Athena::invoke_and_record`, `build_slots_record`, `slotted_cargo_commands`, `AnyRecord::parse`, and the `athena build-slot` binary. All exist except `Slot::held`, `build_slots`, `build_slots_record` and `slotted_cargo_commands`, added in steps 1, 2, 5 and 6. Fixtures: the status test builders (`landed_job_with_waits` pattern, status.rs:3371) and the Invocation helper (status.rs:2429); a real queue in a temp dir; the invocation.rs fake driver. The test writes the log file; the code that reads it is production code.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the design doc, docs/records.md and CHANGELOG. Step 4 of section 8 ends with a 'Built' note stating: the choices (symlink wrapper on argv[0]; settings and log files; the re-entrancy marker and that tests scrub it; pass-through when the settings variable is absent; the slotted list including doc and run; the env-read producer rule and the PATH-resolution check; the optional `build_slots` record with a log line for every slotted command, an honest `slotted_seen` counted with the policy tokenizer, and the status-side fake-driver skip; the per-command peak); the class number (the code's `Class::Producer` = 2 against the design's count from 1); the wait cap and why (1800 s configured, 540 s written with the shipped Bash timeout), that the cap covers only the default Bash timeout and the tool also kills a command that runs long after a win; the ageing consequence (cap below build_age_promote_s 600, no promotion, retries get fresh tickets) and why age carry across retries was not built; why invocation.rs, reading.rs, pr_check.rs, reconcile.rs, landing_tests.rs and docs/records.md changed; and what was not measured or is a known cost: priority-tier ordering of producer requests; no run-level hold is built, so a producer command that times out holds nothing and the producer decides; the peak is a lower bound; `cargo run` and `cargo test` hold a slot for the whole program run; verifier cargo, baseline and reruns unslotted; cargo's children if the wrapper alone is SIGKILLed; whether the host's hook and Bash tool resolve PATH the same way; the unslotted count can overcount only for a killed invocation. docs/records.md gets one sentence on `build_slots`. CHANGELOG Unreleased names the build-slot subcommand, the exit 75 message, the wait cap, the `build_slots` field, the status line, and that a timed-out producer command holds nothing.
demonstrations.observes: A 'Built' note under step 4, a records.md sentence and a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks on the final tree. This builds every Invocation literal (invocation.rs x2, status.rs, pr_check.rs, reconcile.rs, landing_tests.rs) and runs `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`, which compiles unchanged because `Policy` has no new field. The corpus covers reading and plan shapes, not tool-policy forms.
demonstrations.command: cargo test --locked && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo fmt --all --check
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass, no clippy warnings, formatting clean, only Rust and markdown files changed.
demonstrations.fails_without: A compile error from a missed literal or a lint (unused import, too many arguments) fails these.

open_questions: User: The request says the job is 'held, not failed' when no slot frees, but design section 4 (agent-and-build-slots.md:164-165) leaves the decision to the producer after exit 75. The plan builds the design's version (no run-level hold for producer commands) and says so in the Built note and CHANGELOG. Do you want a real hold for a producer whose command times out? That needs job-state access from the wrapper or a driver-level mapping, and edits to the out-of-scope step-3 files.

User: With the shipped config the producer's wait is capped at 540 s, below build_age_promote_s (600 s), so a producer ticket cannot age into the check class and a steady stream of checks can starve it to exit 75. Do you want a governance job to set build_age_promote_s below the cap (for example 300 s) or raise the Bash timeouts in athena.toml (not touched here)? Age carry across retries was considered and not built (decision 6).

User: Should producer requests be ordered by the job's priority tier (urgent, then high, then the rest) as design section 4 describes? The plan leaves it out: the queue has one producer class ordered by time asked, and step 4 of section 8 does not name it.
User: Should the verifier's own cargo commands (verifier_commands, athena.toml:76) also be wrapped? The request says producer commands only; the plan leaves them out and says so in the Built note.

Host: Does the PreToolUse hook process run with the same PATH and environment as Claude Code's Bash tool, or does a shell profile snapshot put another cargo first? Nothing in the repository shows it. The hook's PATH rule and the status note on unslotted cargo commands are how a difference would appear.
